# Worklog pane startup panic misdiagnoses the cause and prescribes the wrong fix

## User story

As a developer hitting a Worklog pane startup failure, I want the panic message
to name the real cause and the command that actually fixes it, so I do not waste
time on a fix that cannot work.

## Problem

`formatStartupError` in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` treats **every**
"does not provide an export named" error as a stale `@worklog/shared`, printing:

```
The plugin loaded a STALE copy of the shared Worklog code:
  The requested module './downtime-worker.constants.js' does not provide an export named 'DEFAULT_COORDINATION_STALE_WINDOW_MS'
This usually means `packages/shared/dist` was built before the current source.
Rebuild and re-link from the repository root:
      npm run build
```

In the incident that prompted this item the missing module was a **local herdr
module** (`./downtime-worker.constants.js`), not `@worklog/shared`. `npm run
build` at the repo root does **not** compile `packages/herdr`, so the prescribed
fix could never have worked. Two rebuild attempts were made before the real
cause (a bad merge resolution) was found.

The message is well-intentioned but its diagnosis is unconditional, and it is
the only guidance an operator gets.

## Desired change

- Distinguish the specifier: an `@worklog/shared` import → keep the current
  stale-shared guidance; a **relative** import → the plugin's own source and
  build output disagree, so prescribe the herdr package build
  (`npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, or the `typecheck` script from the
  sibling prevention item).
- Keep the message actionable and short, and never claim a single cause when the
  evidence does not support it.
- Cover both branches with unit tests (sharing/source mismatch vs local module).

## Acceptance criteria

- A local (relative-specifier) missing-export error names `packages/herdr` and
  the herdr package build command that exists today
  (`npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`); it does not name `packages/shared`
  and does not prescribe the repo-root `npm run build`.
- An `@worklog/shared` missing-export error keeps naming the shared package and
  keeps the existing repo-root `npm run build` guidance.
- All three kinds are unit-tested: shared, local, and unattributable/other-bare
  (which must claim no single cause); the non-missing-export branch is unit-
  tested as unchanged too.
- No regression in the existing launcher behaviour (the launcher still exits
  non-zero, and the pane stays open on a TTY so the message can be read).

## Impact

A startup failure now points at the real cause and the command that fixes it,
instead of sending the user down a dead end.

## Discovered from

Diagnosing a Worklog pane startup failure caused by code dropped in merge
`485b764c7`.
## Plan (2026-11-17)

Planning verdict: **no decomposition.** The change is one pure formatter
function in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` plus its tests and docs (~8 h with
overheads), so the plan is the ordered work sequence below rather than child
work items — the same shape as its completed sibling WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q and
its open sibling WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, neither of which carries children.

### Existing state (verified on the working tree, 2026-11-17)

- `formatStartupError` (`packages/herdr/src/start.ts`) sets `isMissingExport`
  from `/does not provide an export named/i` and emits the **shared-only**
  diagnosis (stale `@worklog/shared`, repo-root `npm run build`). Every other
  failure takes the generic branch (original message + `npm run build` hint +
  `npm install --prefix packages/herdr` fallback).
- The specifier **is** present in the error text and is machine-readable. Node
  22 and tsx 4.21 under `"type": "module"` (as in `packages/herdr`) emit exactly:
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named 'MISSING'`
  — single-quoted specifier, verified against the real resolver by probe.
- Existing coverage: `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (canonical suite)
  already unit-tests the formatter's shared branch and drives the real launcher
  end-to-end against `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-entry.ts` (plus
  `stale-shared.mjs`), asserting exit code 1 and the diagnostic. That harness is
  reusable verbatim for a relative-specifier case: a sibling
  `local-partial.mjs` + `stale-local-entry.ts` pair reproduces
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named ...`
  under tsx (verified).
- `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` resolves to the herdr package
  (`npm prefix --prefix packages/herdr` → `<repo>/packages/herdr`) and runs its
  `build` script (`build:shared` → `tsc` → copy shortcuts + chmod), so the
  prescribed command exists and does compile the plugin. The repo-root
  `npm run build` compiles only root `src/**` and `packages/shared` — it never
  compiles `packages/herdr`.

### Decisions (recorded; conservative, no producer input required)

- **D1 — prescribe only commands that exist.** The local-branch message
  prescribes `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`; it does **not** reference
  the root `typecheck` script from WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, because that script does
  not exist yet (`jq .scripts.typecheck package.json` → absent) — naming it
  would reproduce this very defect. AC1 is refined accordingly.
- **D2 — classify by the specifier, not by the module that failed.** Three
  kinds: `shared` (`@worklog/shared…`), `local` (`.`, `..` or an absolute path)
  and `unknown` (no specifier could be extracted, or another bare package). A
  single cause is claimed only for `shared` and `local`.
- **D3 — the launcher contract is unchanged.** `launch()` keeps exit code 1,
  stderr and the TTY-gated keep-open; only the text of the diagnostic changes
  (AC4).
- **D4 — keep the message short.** ≤ ~10 lines per branch, always carrying the
  original error detail verbatim.
- **D5 — no decomposition** (see the verdict above). Test-first ordering is the
  four phases below.

### Message contract (implementation target)

| Kind | Evidence in the error text | Diagnosis | Prescribed command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shared` | specifier begins `@worklog/shared` | stale shared build (text unchanged) | `npm run build` (repo root) |
| `local` | specifier begins `./`, `../` or `/` | the plugin's own module and its build output disagree — names `packages/herdr` | `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` |
| `unknown` | no quoted specifier, or a different bare package | no single cause is claimed; both rebuilds offered | both commands |

The `local` text must state explicitly that the repo-root `npm run build` does
not compile the plugin (the trap that cost the incident two rebuild attempts),
and the `unknown` text must claim neither a stale shared build nor a stale local
build.

### Ordered work sequence (test-first)

1. **Phase 1 — RED tests** in `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (the
   `formatStartupError` describe block):
   - relative specifier → names `packages/herdr`, contains
     `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, and contains neither
     `STALE copy of the shared Worklog code` nor `packages/shared/dist`;
   - `@worklog/shared` specifier → shared guidance unchanged (anti-regression);
   - unattributable / other-bare specifier → no single-cause wording, both
     commands present;
   - non-missing-export error → generic branch unchanged (existing assertion);
   - non-`Error` throw → unchanged (existing assertion).

   Verify: the new assertions are RED and every currently-green assertion stays
   green.
2. **Phase 2 — implementation** in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`:
   - extract the quoted specifier (`/The requested module ['"]([^'"]+)['"]/i`,
     tolerant of both quote styles; an absent match yields `unknown`) and
     classify it;
   - branch the message per the table; leave `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()` and
     the entry-point detection untouched.

   Verify: Phase 1 green; the existing shared-branch and e2e tests stay green.
3. **Phase 3 — end-to-end fixture.** Add
   `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` (exports only a different
   name) and `stale-local-entry.ts` (imports a missing name from
   `./local-partial.mjs`), then extend the `pane launcher (src/start.ts,
   end-to-end)` block: exit code 1, the relative-specifier diagnostic, the herdr
   build command, and prompt exit with stdin closed (the AC4 keep-open
   behaviour is TTY-gated, so the closed-stdin case must not hang).

   Verify: the new e2e case is RED before Phase 2's formatter change and green
   after it.
4. **Phase 4 — docs.** `packages/herdr/README.md` § *Development* (the
   `src/start.ts` note) and § *The Worklog tab closes immediately on open*
   (Troubleshooting): describe both causes, both commands, and that the
   repo-root build does not compile the plugin. Update the `start.ts` header
   comment, which currently presents the stale-shared case as the only cause.

   Verify: no remaining text claims the shared build is the only cause
   (`grep -rin "stale copy of the shared" packages/herdr/`).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` — the formatter and its header comment.
- `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` — formatter unit tests + launcher e2e.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` — new fixture module.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-local-entry.ts` — new fixture entry.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Development + Troubleshooting wording.

### Constraints

- Do not change `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()`, the entry-point detection, the
  TTY gating or the exit code (AC4).
- Do not add a dependency or a new command script: the fix is message text plus
  a specifier classifier.
- Do not weaken the existing shared-branch text — the shared case is still
  correct, and its tests are the anti-regression guard.
- Do not reference the not-yet-existing root `typecheck` script (D1).

### Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — error-text drift across Node versions.** Node 22 quotes the specifier
  with `'`; a future version could change the phrasing. *Mitigation:* the
  extractor tolerates both quote styles and treats an unmatched specifier as
  `unknown`, which claims no single cause — still correct, just less specific.
- **R2 — tsx resolves TS specifiers (`.js` → `.ts`).** The incident specifier was
  a relative `.js` naming a `.ts` source; both are relative, so classification is
  unaffected. *Mitigation:* fixtures use `.mjs` (as the existing shared fixture
  does), which the ESM linker checks without rewriting — verified with tsx 4.21.
- **A1 — `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` is the right prescription.**
  Verified: the herdr `build` script exists and `--prefix` resolves from the repo
  root; it compiles `packages/shared` first, so it repairs both a stale plugin
  build and a stale shared build.
- **A2 — the new assertions are gate-enforced.** `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts`
  is in the canonical suite (`tests`), so no change to `groups.herdr` is needed.

### Out of scope

- Making the repo-root `npm run build` compile `packages/herdr`, and adding a
  root `typecheck` script — WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV.
- Changing the pane-launch manifest or herdr's own error reporting.
- Any change to the `@worklog/shared` link/refresh mechanics — WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
  owns that.

### Dependencies

- None blocking. `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` exists today, so this
  item does not wait on WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV.
- Once WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV lands, that item's docs may additionally advertise the
  root `typecheck`; no code change here is required.

### Duplicate-work check

No overlapping open or completed item. `wl search` on startup / herdr /
typecheck / "export named" returned: WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A (restore the code a bad
merge dropped, completed — the incident, not the diagnostic), WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
(added the launcher and its shared-only diagnostic, completed — its AC3 covers
only a *shared* export, so its ACs are not satisfied here),
WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4 (missing `marked` package, completed — a different error
class) and WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV (the typecheck gate, open — sibling).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — plan pass (agent, non-interactive downtime dispatch): added this
  plan block, the message contract, the four-phase test-first work sequence, Key
  Files, constraints, risks, out-of-scope, dependencies and the duplicate-work
  check. Refined AC1 (the `typecheck` alternative is not prescribed because the
  script does not exist — D1), AC2 (names the existing root command explicitly)
  and AC3/AC4 ("all three kinds"; exit-code plus TTY keep-open). No children
  created (D5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Should the message prescribe the root `typecheck` script from the
  sibling prevention item, as the Desired change's parenthetical suggests?**
  Answer (agent, documented decision): **No — prescribe
  `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` only.** Evidence:
  `jq .scripts.typecheck package.json` → absent (WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV is
  `plan_complete`, not implemented), so naming it would send the operator to a
  command that does not exist — the exact failure this item fixes. Status:
  resolved by evidence. Reopen only if the producer wants forward references to
  unlanded scripts (not recommended).

- **Q2 — Is a third ("unknown") branch in scope, or should only the shared and
  relative cases change?** Answer (agent, documented decision): **In scope.** The
  Desired change requires "never claim a single cause when the evidence does not
  support it", so a missing-export error from another bare specifier — or one
  whose specifier the extractor cannot read — must hedge. Encoded in AC3.

- **Q3 — Does the plan need child features?** Answer (agent, documented
  decision): **No.** One pure function plus tests and docs (~8 h with
  overheads), and both items of the same shape (WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q,
  WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV) carry zero children. Test-first ordering is the four
  phases above.

- **Q4 — Is there duplicate work in flight?** Answer (agent): **No** — see the
  duplicate-work check above.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSG6ODD5002X2OF** – Wire postbuild hook and update docs (completed)
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** – herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find package 'marked' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: acceptance, actionable, actually, attempts, bad (+113 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, actionable, actually, attempts, bad (+113 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: actionable, actually, behaviour, build, cannot (+96 more)

# Fairness across remote dispatching hosts

Investigation item: **examine why one machine obtains a disproportionate share
of the shared dispatch slots when several hosts dispatch at once, and present
potential solutions.** The deliverable is an evidence-backed RCA plus an options
paper with one recommendation — implementation is deferred to follow-up items
(including a cross-repo proxy item where required).

## Problem statement

When more than one host runs downtime dispatchers against the same shared
llama-proxy, one machine consistently holds an unfair share of the scarce local
GPU slots: its panes occupy slot time while other hosts' dispatchable work waits
or is never dispatched. The suspicion is that the winning host is simply the one
running more dispatcher instances / agent panes, because slot arbitration is
keyed to the **session**, not to the **host** — so a host's share grows with the
number of sessions it happens to have live.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle capacity shared across hosts on a rule I can
  state and verify, so that a machine running many dispatchers does not
  monopolise the GPU slot budget at the expense of a machine running one.
- **As a project owner whose work sits on a starved host**, I want to see from
  the logs *why* my host got no slot (host-share, lease retention, budget, or a
  safety gate) rather than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness invariant enforced (or
  at least measured and documented) by the code path that actually grants a
  slot, with a way to detect regression from the recorded evidence.
- **As the proxy maintainer**, I want any host-aware arbitration to reuse the
  existing lease/queue machinery and the existing client-identity logging,
  without adding a second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented
  window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host,
  dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle)
  lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with
  `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact
  queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- A root-cause analysis names every mechanism that can push a host's share above
  a fair share, with code references and evidence, or rules it out with
  evidence. At minimum evaluate: (a) session-keyed lease acquisition with
  same-session re-acquisition and non-preemptive idle-lease retention; (b) a
  host's share scaling with its number of dispatcher instances / live panes;
  (c) the free-slot gate reading one global slot snapshot, so the earliest or
  fastest poller wins; (d) the absence of any host-keyed slot accounting today.
- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it
  treats hosts with **different numbers of dispatcher instances** (the
  invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and
  hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no
  dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming
  the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure
  modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change
  (a new `LP-` work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must
  include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- One recommendation is made — the smallest change that makes host share
  independent of instance count — with its residual risks and the follow-up
  work items required to implement it recorded and linked (this item does not
  implement it).
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the report is reproducible from a
  documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the
  measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- Fairness cannot regress the existing dispatch gates: critical-first,
  review-queue depth, code-freeze, host-CPU gate, host dispatch budget and the
  audit tier must be shown to behave exactly as today (by inspection of the
  proposed change surface, since this item ships no behaviour change).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator can see, host by host, how shared dispatch capacity is actually
distributed and why one machine dominates — and gets a single change that makes
each host's share depend on the work it has, not on how many dispatchers happen
to be running there.

## Constraints

- **Investigation, not a scheduler rewrite.** Deliver measured evidence, a
  fairness definition, options and one recommendation. Record implementation as
  follow-up items rather than doing it here.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** Proxy arbitration lives in `llm-manager` (`LP-`
  prefix, e.g. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`); herdr-side work must not assume a
  new proxy contract exists. Any host-aware arbitration that must run in the
  proxy needs its own `LP-` work item and a version-tolerant client.
- **Fail-open.** Any new accounting or arbitration must never refuse a dispatch
  because a read, lock or log parse failed; a failure degrades to today's
  behaviour.
- **Hot-path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; measurement runs
  off-log, not in the dispatch loop.
- **Gates preserved.** Critical-first, review-queue, code-freeze, host-CPU gate,
  host dispatch budget and audit admission keep their current precedence;
  fairness never buys itself by relaxing a safety gate.
- **No unilateral cap changes.** Changing per-host `budget.json` defaults
  (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size` is
  a producer decision; the options paper must quantify such a change rather than
  apply it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: wrong resource.** If "slots" turns out not to be the proxy's local
  slots, the measurement AC still surfaces the real contention point (AC1
  requires both slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host); the options
  paper must then address whatever the data shows.
- **Risk: measurement needs a quiet or attributable window.** Proxy logs carry
  `client_ip`, but a `local-preferred` request routed to a remote provider never
  holds a local slot, so slot-seconds and dispatch counts must be reported
  separately to avoid a misleading ratio.
- **Risk: proxy change is a separate release train.** A host-aware lease needs
  an `LP-` item and a version-tolerant herdr client; the dispatcher-side option
  is the fallback if the proxy change stalls.
- **Risk: fairness versus throughput.** Per-host caps can idle the GPU when one
  host has all the work; the options paper must quantify the idle cost of each
  option rather than trading throughput silently.
- **Scope-creep guard:** fixing per-host fairness in code, changing
  `budget.json` defaults, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, or building a
  dashboard is **out of scope** — record each as a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A1–A4** are recorded in the appendix and need producer
  confirmation at review; none blocks starting the investigation.

## Existing state

- **Dispatch-side fairness is per machine, by construction.** The coordination
  dir, leader election and dispatch-budget ledger are single-machine
  (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, `machine-coordination.ts`); the docs state the local
  coordination/ledger paths are single-machine and that only the audit budget is
  cross-machine, via the proxy. Per-host caps today are `maxImplement: 2` /
  legacy `maxAudit: 1` in `budget.json`.
- **The genuinely shared resource across hosts is the proxy's local slots.** The
  dispatcher's free-slot gate reads one **global** slot snapshot from
  `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`; whoever polls and dispatches first takes
  the slot.
- **Slot arbitration is session-keyed, not host-keyed.**
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch(srv, max_local, session_key, …)` admits up to
  `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent sessions; same-session re-acquisition is
  always permitted, and the no-preemption policy lets an inactive (post-request
  cooldown) lease keep reserving its slot for the owning session. Nothing in the
  lease record names the host.
- **Host attribution exists only in logs.** The proxy resolves and logs
  `client_ip` / `client_ip_source` / `client_port` on status and lease events
  (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88), so per-host slot-seconds are measurable after the fact,
  but no arbitration or accounting path consumes host identity.
- **Per-project rotation already exists and is single-machine.** The
  least-recently-served root ordering with a twice-in-succession run-length
  bound (`downtime-worker.fairness.ts`, WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 /
  WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O) fixes *project* concentration on one host; it has no
  notion of a host and cannot arbitrate across machines.
- **Prior attribution incident.** A 2026-08 investigation (WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T)
  found ~8 un-attributable `status_request` pollers, 3–4 concurrent connections
  from a single remote host; client-IP logging was added as the fix. That is the
  precedent for measuring rather than guessing.

## Desired change

A published report (e.g. `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md`, linked from
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) containing: the per-host share measurement
and its methodology, the fairness definition and invariant, the root-cause
findings with code references, the candidate solutions with trade-offs and a
recommendation, and links to the follow-up implementation items. No behaviour
change in this item.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` — new report: measurement, fairness definition, root causes, options, recommendation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — cross-host fairness section/link; correct any "single-machine only" wording that measurement contradicts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-cpu-gate.ts` — global free-slot gate (candidate dispatcher-side lever); inspect for the host-count interaction, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — per-host ledger/caps (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`) referenced by the options paper, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine-scope contract and its doc comment (any wording change)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability surface, candidate place to surface host share
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — per-project rotation (contrast: why it cannot arbitrate across hosts)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` session-keyed leases (proxy-side option; cross-repo `LP-` item)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `_resolve_client_ip` / `_resolve_client_id`, the host-attribution seam used for measurement
- `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — existing fairness discussion (per-session FIFO), the design context for any proxy-side option

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (completed) — dispatcher unevenly distributes work
  across *projects* on one machine; measured the same class of concentration and
  produced the round-robin/run-length fixes. This item is the cross-*host*
  analogue and must reuse its measurement style.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** (completed) — whole-set rotation with a run-length
  bound; establishes the "no new scheduler" precedent.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — post-dispatch cursor charge; how the
  previous fairness defect was diagnosed from decision logs.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** (completed) — over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM:
  per-tick free-slot polling versus the proxy owner lease. Closest existing
  analysis of slot-vs-dispatch accounting.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** (completed) — host-wide audit slot saturation from
  concurrent audits; the precedent that a shared proxy resource needs
  cross-instance coordination.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (completed) — proxy-owned audit budget: the one
  existing cross-machine serialisation pattern to imitate or extend.
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** (completed) — poller attribution on proxy:8000;
  produced the `client_ip` logging this measurement depends on.
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** (completed) — dispatch logs/leases on the remote
  host filesystem; where per-host dispatch evidence lives.
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** (completed) — truthful per-slot capacity consumption
  (`lease_state` / `capacity_hint`), the semantics of "a slot" in this codebase.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across
  multiple projects not working; the earlier defect family this item must not
  re-litigate for the per-host case.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** (completed) — docs for the enforced fair-scheduling
  rule and its metric; the documented-metric precedent to follow.
- **llm-manager `LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88`** (proxy) — client-identity logging
  (completed proxy side); the attribution prerequisite.
- **docs**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (host budget, proxy-derived audit
  admission, free-slot gate), `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime settings),
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` and
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/contention-queue-*.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was dispatched automatically by the herdr downtime worker
(`herdr-downtime`, session id recorded on the work item), so no interactive
producer round was available. Questions are recorded below with the documented
assumption used and marked for producer confirmation at review; none of them
blocks the investigation this item scopes.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" here — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or
  the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**
  (llama-server slots / local dispatch leases). Rationale: "slot" is used that
  way throughout `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ("free-slot gate", "slot
  budget", `lease_state`), the dispatch budget is already per-host, and the only
  resource that is genuinely shared across hosts is the proxy GPU. AC1 requires
  measuring **both** slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host, so the
  analysis identifies the real contention point instead of assuming it.
  Source: repo search (`packages/herdr/src`, `llm-manager/proxy`).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Is the deliverable a report with proposed solutions, or a code change?
  — Answer (agent, from the item description): the description says "examine why
  this is and present potential solutions", so the deliverable is an
  evidence-backed RCA plus an options paper with one recommendation; the
  code change is recorded as follow-up work items. Source: item description.
  Status: accepted; revisit at review if the producer wants the fix in scope.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy
  change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed, but at least one option must be
  dispatcher-side, and any proxy change must be split into its own `LP-` item
  because this is a `WL-` (ContextHub) work item and the repos are separate.
  Source: repo boundary evidence (`llm-manager` has its own `LP-` worklog).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of
  dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant to hold is that a host's share must
  **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline,
  with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit alternative. The options paper
  quantifies both. Source: item description ("different machines may have
  different numbers of the dispatcher running").
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared
  proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) and any remote
  host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Source:
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (proxy default), WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T (remote host
  evidence). Status: recorded; the window is chosen in the report.

## Goal

Collect per-host slot usage data from the llama-proxy structured logs and dispatcher logs for one documented window with at least two participating hosts, producing a reproducible table of per-host metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host, dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle) lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the measurable output is reproducible from a documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- The measurement window is documented: dates, hosts, proxy URL, and the exact conditions under which the window was captured.
- Per-host table columns are populated: dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle) lease time, share of total.
- The exact queries/commands used to produce the table are documented and can be reproduced by an auditor.
- The measurement runs off-log, not in the dispatch loop (hot-path budget constraint satisfied).
- Fail-open: a missing, unreadable or unparseable log degrades to "not measurable" in the report — the measurement never refuses or blocks a dispatch.

## Deliverables

- Measurement script or query set (with unit test if a script is created)
- Per-host share table for one documented window
- Documentation of data sources and reproduction steps

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — coordination/decision log entry shape and readers (per-host dispatch evidence)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — dispatch-log entry shapes and fail-safe reader
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — machine-scoped ledger and `dispatch-budget.log` audit trail
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability reduction to reuse
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — coordination dir resolution (`dispatch-budget.json`, `dispatch-budget.log`)
- `scripts/measure-host-slot-share.ts` — new measurement helper reducing proxy/lease logs into per-host slot-seconds (with a colocated `scripts/measure-host-slot-share.test.ts` unit test)

# Stale scratch worktrees make the implement foreign-change-surface guard refuse clean children

## Problem Statement

The `implement` skill's foreign-change-surface guard (`_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`) fails `parent`/`start`/`finish` closed for a non-terminal child whose own worktree holds no changes, whenever **any** registered sibling worktree of the same repository is dirty. The precision rule ("the dirt is only evidence if the work is not in the child's worktree") is right, but the set of surfaces it scans includes long-dead debris: scratch worktrees registered under `/tmp` from old manual checks, and leftover trees belonging to work items that are already `completed`/`deleted`. Because that debris never changes, every subsequent clean child in that checkout is refused until an operator removes the trees by hand.

Observed during the epic drive `WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB` (`2026-11-21T10:52Z` and `11:12Z`): after a driven child session died, `parent` refused the next child's **clean** worktree and named four unrelated surfaces — three `/tmp/wl-*` scratch trees and the leftover worktree of the already-`deleted` item `WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG` — so the epic chain could only continue after manual `git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`.

## Users

- **Operators driving epics.** As an operator, I want a clean child worktree to be admitted by `parent`/`start`/`finish` even when my checkout still carries old scratch worktrees, so an epic chain does not stall on debris that predates the run.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the unattended dispatcher, I want the guard's refusals to mean "a session really wrote outside its worktree", so an auto-dispatched epic does not park itself waiting for a human to prune `/tmp`.
- **Framework maintainer.** As the maintainer of the guard, I want remaining foreign-surface detection to stay intact (a child that really strays into another live item's worktree must still fail closed), and I want the debris to be *reported* by the hygiene path with an exact remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered sibling worktree **outside** the repository's worktree root (e.g. under `/tmp`) with pre-existing dirt no longer blocks `parent`/`start`/`finish` for a clean child worktree — it is never treated as a foreign change surface, dirty or not.
- A leftover worktree whose **owning work item is terminal** (`completed`, `in_review`, `done`, `deleted`) does not block a different item's clean child, wherever it lives.
- Genuine cross-worktree writes are still detected: a dirty registered sibling **inside** the worktree root whose owning item is **non-terminal** still fails the run closed with the actionable message naming the sibling and its paths, and the existing `SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I` / `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G` tests stay green. Ownership that cannot be resolved (no work-item id in the path, or `wl show` unavailable) stays **fail-closed**.
- The hygiene path offers a documented remedy for the debris: `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports (a) registered worktrees outside the repository's worktree root and (b) worktrees whose owning work item is terminal, in both text and `--json` output, and prints the prune remedy (`git worktree remove <path> && git worktree prune`). Existing checks, exit codes and warning semantics are unchanged, and the remedy is documented in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Tests: new unit tests cover the surface filter (outside-root sibling ignored, terminal-owner sibling ignored, live-owner sibling still refuses, unresolved ownership fails closed, child with its own work never refused) and the new hygiene checks; existing guard tests are unmodified and green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

An epic drive no longer stalls because of old scratch worktrees lying around the checkout: a clean child is admitted, while a session that genuinely wrote into another live item's worktree is still caught — and the hygiene check now tells the operator exactly which stale trees to prune.

## Constraints

- **Delivery target is the SorraAgents framework repo** (the guard lives in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the hygiene script in `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`; the canonical docs in `docs/dev/`). ContextHub's own `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents ContextHub-local mechanisms and is **not** an edit target. Work is tracked in the ContextHub worklog, so `wl` commands must run against the ContextHub worklog dir.
- **Never destructive.** The fix must not delete, prune or reset any worktree automatically — not the child's, not a sibling's. Removal stays an operator decision (the framework forbids deleting trees/stashes without explicit permission); the guard only stops *counting* debris as evidence.
- **Preserve precision and fail-closed defaults.** The child's own worktree holding work continues to short-circuit the whole check; unreadable/unparseable ownership fails closed (never silently ignored) for inside-root siblings.
- **Bounded cost.** The added worklog lookup runs only for dirty inside-root siblings of a child whose own worktree is clean — the guard's current fast paths (child worktree carries work; no dirty siblings) must not gain a `wl` subprocess.
- Scope excludes the `reset-for-retry` behaviour (a worktree with commits ahead is already refused and uncommitted WIP is already snapshotted/reported) and excludes any change to `implement.py start`'s dirty-main-checkout gate.

## Existing State

Guard code (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`):

- `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths(worktree_path, repo_root)` (≈L20182) returns **every** existing registered worktree of `repo_root` except the main checkout and the child's own — with no path-scope and no item-state filter.
- `_child_main_checkout_violation(...)` (≈L20383) builds `sibling_offending` from all those siblings via `_git_path_has_changes(...)`; call sites are `phase_parent` (≈L15844, ≈L15905) and, transitively, `phase_drive`/`start`.
- `_worktree_placement_violation(...)` (≈L20248, call site `phase_finish` ≈L12760) does the same for the cwd-sensitive case, plus `_sibling_worktree_containing(...)` (≈L20223) which is likewise unfiltered.
- Existing exemptions: work in the child's own worktree; recorded spawn-failure evidence (`read_spawn_failure`, `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`); no dirty surface at all.
- Helpers that already exist and make the fix cheap: `wl_show()` (≈L897), `_is_terminal_child()`, and `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review","completed","done","deleted"}` (≈L1761). No reverse helper exists yet to derive a work item id from a worktree path; paths are deterministic (`<worktree-dir>/wl-<WORK-ITEM-ID>-<slug>`, plus `audit-exec-<WORK-ITEM-ID>` trees).

Debris confirmed present in the ContextHub checkout at intake time (`git worktree list`):

| Path | Owner | State | Why it is debris |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/tmp/wl-base-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `/tmp/wl-clean-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `/tmp/wl-dev-head-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-extract-createdowntimedeps-into-its-own` | `WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG` | `deleted`; dirty (`index.ts`, `index.downtime-deps*.ts`) | leftover tree of a terminal item |

`scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (SorraAgents) already exists (511 lines, `--json`, exit 0/1/2) and its "orphaned worktrees" check only reports worktrees whose **branch was deleted** — so none of the four debris entries above are reported today (three are detached, one still has its branch).

## Desired Change

1. Introduce a **live foreign surface** filter used by all three placement checks: a registered sibling counts only when (a) its path lies inside the repository's worktree root (`.worklog/worktrees/` by default) **and** (b) its owning work item resolves and is **non-terminal**. Untagged/outside-root trees are debris: never evidence.
2. Add a small reverse helper that maps a worktree path to its owning work item id (`wl-<ID>-<slug>`, `audit-exec-<ID>`); unresolved ownership inside the root keeps the current fail-closed behaviour.
3. Keep every existing exemption and message; the refusal text should name the sibling **and** say when stale debris was skipped (one informational log line), so an operator can see why a previously-blocking tree no longer blocks.
4. Extend `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` with the two new reports (outside-root registered worktrees; terminal-owner worktrees) and the printed prune remedy, keeping the existing JSON shape additive and the exit-code contract unchanged.
5. Update the docs: the placement-gate section of `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, the guard lines in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, the hygiene-gate section of `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, and the module docstrings of the touched functions.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths`, `_sibling_worktree_containing`, `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`; new reverse worktree→item helper and the live-surface filter.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — new outside-root and terminal-owner worktree reports plus the prune remedy (`check_orphaned_worktrees`, ≈L226).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — extend with the debris-filter matrix (existing 17 tests unchanged).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` — placement-gate parity for the same filter.
- `tests/test_implement_stash_hygiene.py` — hygiene-script tests (existing file already asserts the script's existence/`--json`/help contract).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — placement-gate and hygiene-remedy sections.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guard description of record.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — hygiene gate paragraph (`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** "outside the repository's worktree root" means the configured worktree directory (`DEFAULT_WORKTREE_DIR`, `.worklog/worktrees/`), so `/tmp` scratch trees — including audit trees created under `/tmp` — are excluded by construction; noted because `/tmp` trees are also how some audits run.
- **Assumption:** resolving terminality with one `wl show` per dirty inside-root sibling is acceptable (bounded by the number of registered worktrees, and never reached on the fast paths) and inherits `--worklog-dir` resolution via `resolve_worklog_flags`.
- **Risk (mitigated):** the filter could hide a genuine stray write into a tree whose owning item is terminal — accepted, because that item's session is over and cannot be raced; the write surfaces that matter are `dev` and live children.
- **Risk (mitigated):** `wl show` unavailable/slow in a git-only environment → unreadable ownership fails closed, and the check is skipped entirely when no inside-root sibling is dirty.
- **Risk:** the hygiene script's new checks may report the maintainers' own long-lived trees — mitigated by reporting only (no exit-code change for the existing checks beyond the documented warning path).
- **Scope-creep risk:** an operator may ask for automatic pruning of these trees; that is a separate destructive-behaviour decision and must be filed as its own work item, not folded in here.

## Related Work

- `SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I` (completed) — *implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red*: introduced the sibling-worktree surface check this item narrows.
- `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G` (completed) — *spawn-failed child with no-work worktree should not trigger placement violation*: the most recent precedent for an evidence-based exemption in the same guard.
- `SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5` (completed) — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as "has changes": same theme, worktree change-detection precision.
- `SA-0MT4DFE8Y004J8SP` (completed) — added `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` and the stash hygiene gate (the script this item extends; the id no longer resolves in the worklog, evidence is commit `80dbf5a230`).
- `SA-0MUG216UP008821M` (completed) — *Clean up fixture artefacts left in the live SorraAgents checkout by the test-isolation incident*: precedent for debris-cleanup items being separate from guard fixes.
- `WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB` (in_review, epic) — where the refusal was observed; its children `WL-0MWF34932000SNTX` (F2) were refused repeatedly for exactly this debris.

# Implement live foreign surface filter in implement.py

## Description
Introduce a live foreign surface filter in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` used by all placement checks (`_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`, `_sibling_worktree_containing`).

- New reverse helper `_worktree_path_to_item_id(path)` mapping `wl-<ID>-<slug>` and `audit-exec-<ID>` directory names to work-item IDs.
- New debris predicates: outside-root (cheap path check) and terminal-owner (one `wl show` per dirty inside-root sibling).
- Keep `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths` raw; call sites skip debris cheap-first so the fast paths gain no `wl` subprocess.
- Preserve every existing exemption/message; emit one informational log line when debris is skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A registered sibling worktree **outside** the repository's worktree root (e.g. under `/tmp`) with pre-existing dirt no longer blocks `parent`/`start`/`finish` for a clean child worktree — it is never treated as a foreign change surface, dirty or not.
- A leftover worktree whose **owning work item is terminal** (`completed`, `in_review`, `done`, `deleted`) does not block a different item's clean child, wherever it lives.
- Genuine cross-worktree writes are still detected: a dirty registered sibling **inside** the worktree root whose owning item is **non-terminal** still fails the run closed with the actionable message naming the sibling and its paths.
- Ownership that cannot be resolved (no work-item id in the path, or `wl show` unavailable) stays **fail-closed**.
- The added worklog lookup runs only for dirty inside-root siblings; the guard's fast paths (child worktree carries work; no dirty siblings) gain no `wl` subprocess.
- One informational log line is emitted when stale debris is skipped, so an operator sees why a previously-blocking tree no longer blocks.
- Existing guard tests (`test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py`, `test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`) are unmodified and pass.


## Delivery note (test-first merge, 2026-11-21)

The filter itself landed in `WL-0MWQM9MMY008793R` (commit `1c581cefd3`): its
tests and the implementation had to be committed together, because a tests-only
commit cannot pass the build → test → commit gate. This item therefore delivers
the one acceptance criterion that commit did not pin with a test — **AC6, the
informational log line when stale debris is skipped** — as a focused caplog
suite (outside-root skip reported, terminal-owner skip reported, a live dirty
sibling reports no skip), and records the live-checkout verification below.

Verification against the real SorraAgents checkout (read-only) — every dirty
registered sibling classified, `parent`-relevant debris discounted:

- `/tmp/audit-code-root-*`, `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*/wt` → outside the worktree
  root → skipped;
- leftover trees of terminal items (`SA-0MSQRZ5N6005WI43`,
  `SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A`, `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9`, `SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV`,
  `WL-0MVPE2B8E005O0OS`) → terminal owner → skipped;
- dirty siblings of live items still refuse, and an id `wl show` cannot
  resolve (`SA-0MVTUD4HS000O6AB`) stays fail-closed.

## Impact

The guard now says why a tree no longer blocks a clean child, instead of
looking like it silently stopped working.

# ruff DTZ007: naive datetime in `_job_elapsed_seconds` (rss_server.py:2856-2857)

## Problem

Ruff reports DTZ007 — "Naive datetime constructed using `datetime.datetime.strptime()` without `%z`" — on two adjacent lines in `rss_server.py` (`_job_elapsed_seconds` function). The function parses `created_at` / `updated_at` ISO-8601 UTC timestamps to compute wall-clock elapsed seconds. Both datetimes are naive but represent the same UTC epoch, so the subtraction produces correct elapsed seconds. However, the code is inconsistent with the project's broader use of tz-aware datetimes.

## Users

- **Producer / audit system**: needs a consistent decision on whether this narrow, safe pattern is accepted as a false positive (record waiver) or fixed.
- **Future maintainers**: would benefit from consistent datetime handling (tz-aware throughout).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer accepts one of two paths:
   - **Option A — Accept as false positive:** Record an audit waiver via `audit_waiver.py add <audited-item-id> --rule DTZ007 --file src/rss_server.py --justification "…"`. A waiver with no `--line` would cover both lines (2856 and 2857) and prevents re-creation of chores.
   - **Option B — Fix the code:** Replace `strptime` with tz-aware parsing (preferred: `.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))` consistent with existing pattern at line 2216) **or** add `.replace(tzinfo=UTC)` post-parse.
2. If Option B is chosen, apply the same fix to the sibling work item for line 2856 (WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP), or combine into a single fix.
3. The ruff check `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` passes (zero errors) after resolution.

## Impact

Ruff DTZ007 false-positive decision: accept the narrow elapsed-time pattern as a waiver (no code change) or fix the two datetime parses to use tz-aware ISO timestamps, improving consistency with the rest of the project.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change the function's return value (elapsed seconds in float).
- If fixing, the approach must be consistent with the project's existing datetime handling pattern (see line 2216).
- The sibling item (line 2856) shares the same function and should be resolved in the same change.

## Existing state

- Function `_job_elapsed_seconds(job: dict) -> float | None` at line 2845 parses `created_at`/`updated_at` as naive UTC datetimes via `strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")` and returns `(ended - started).total_seconds()`.
- The project imports `from datetime import UTC, datetime` and uses `datetime.now(UTC)` and `datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))` elsewhere.
- Sibling work item WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP (line 2856) — both lines in the same function, same root cause.

## Key Files

- `src/rss_server.py` — `_job_elapsed_seconds` function (lines 2845–2859)

## Related work

- WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP — ruff DTZ007 at line 2856 (same function, sibling finding).
- Line 2216 in `rss_server.py` — existing pattern `dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")` / `datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str)` — candidate for reuse.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The sibling line 2856 item exists separately; should be resolved in the same change but tracked as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** The timestamps are always in the same UTC format; no cross-timezone edge cases.
- **Assumption:** The audit waiver mechanism records on the audited work item (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8), not this chore — the `audit_waiver.py add` command targets the correct item.

# Test: main-checkout churn verdict pins

**Parent:** WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC (pre-push live-repo mutation gate blocks driven finishes).
**Repo boundary:** agent infrastructure — this lands in the **SorraAgents** skill tree
(`skill/shared`, `skill/test`, `tests/`), not ContextHub source. `skill/shared` is a
gitignored symlink in ContextHub pointing at `~/.pi/agent/skills` →
`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`.
**Test-first:** this item is written and made green *before* the rule change in
"Role-scope the guard's verdict surface" lands.

## Why

The producer approved mechanism **(A)**: narrow the **main checkout**'s verdict surface so a
concurrent session's mid-run writes cannot fail a driven child's finish, while the
tracked-file deletion/wipe class (2026-10-26 `packages/shared`) stays verdict-bearing. The
guard is the single outer owner (`guarded_run_all`) plus the inner `live_repo_guard`
pytest plugin, both going through `diff_guarded_roots` → `diff_snapshots`. Nothing currently
pins the role-scoped rule, and the existing clean→dirty pin
(`TestWorkingTreeAttributionBoundaries`) asserts the *unscoped* behaviour.

## Scope

Add characterisation/regression tests **only** (xfail or failing first, then flipped by the
implementation sibling). Cover the shared helper, the outer guard and the inner plugin so the
rule cannot fork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Regression tests cover both directions: (a) a dirty main checkout with a clean child
  worktree ⇒ the gate passes and reports the foreign paths as informational; (b) the suite
  mutating the guarded checkout during the run ⇒ the gate fails and names the paths.
- A dirty main checkout means the shapes actually observed on 2026-11-13: a modified tracked
  file (` M`), an untracked new file (`??`) and a staged modification (`M `) created mid-run
  by a second actor — all three must leave the verdict green.
- The wipe protection is pinned fail-closed: a tracked-file deletion created in the main
  checkout mid-run still fails the run and the message names the path **and** the main
  checkout (extends the existing `test_guarded_run_from_worktree_fails_on_main_checkout_deletion`).
- The guarded root's own rule is unchanged and still pinned: a clean→dirty modification or
  deletion **inside the child worktree** remains a mutation (`TestWorkingTreeAttributionIncidents`
  stays green, unmodified in intent).
- Inner-plugin parity is pinned: `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` proves the
  `live_repo_guard` plugin reaches the same verdict as `guarded_run_all` for both directions
  (no forked rule).
- The actor-attribution fallback is pinned: when no concurrent actor is discoverable the note
  says `unknown` and never fails the run.
- New tests fail before the implementation lands (xfail-marked where the harness requires a
  green tree, strict-xfail removed by the flip) and pass afterwards.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — `TestWorkingTreeAttribution*`,

- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — outer-guard end-to-end:

## Constraints

- Rule and pins move together in one change (the parent's "conflicting documented design

## Impact

Agents and operators stop chasing phantom corruption: a driven child's finish gate stays green when another session is merely writing the shared main checkout, while a genuine tracked-file wipe in that checkout still fails loudly naming the path and the checkout — behaviour now pinned by regression tests so it cannot silently regress.

# Role-scope the guard's verdict surface

**Parent:** WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC. **Depends on:** "Test: main-checkout churn verdict pins".
**Repo boundary:** **SorraAgents** skill tree (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`).

## Why

`diff_snapshots` treats *any* clean→dirty working-tree transition as suite damage. In a
linked-worktree run that surface includes the **shared main checkout**, so a sibling session
writing `.ts` sources mid-run fails an unrelated, clean child (WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR, 2026-11-13).
The producer approved mechanism **(A)**: narrow the main checkout's verdict to the damage class
the suite can plausibly cause, and report the rest as informational.

## The rule (role-scoped, git plumbing only)

Applied in `diff_guarded_roots`, which is the only place that knows each root's `role`, so both
the outer guard and the inner plugin inherit it without forking:

- **Guarded root** (`GUARDED_ROOT_ROLE`, the run's own worktree or a non-linked root) —
  **unchanged**: every clean→dirty modification, deletion or creation is verdict-bearing, and a
  still-dirty path whose code changed is verdict-bearing.
- **Main checkout** (`MAIN_CHECKOUT_ROLE`) — a newly dirty path is verdict-bearing **only** when
  the end status code reports a tracked-file deletion (`D` in either status column). Newly
  modified (` M`, `M `, `MM`), untracked (`??`), staged additions (`A `) and deletion-free code
  transitions are moved to an excluded bucket and reported informationally.
- **Unchanged everywhere:** pre-existing-dirty→clean resolution stays excluded; refs and config
  stay fully verdict-bearing on **both** roots; the per-test fingerprint stays a superset
  trigger (it may still fire on main-checkout churn — the verdict is unaffected).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate distinguishes changes that were pre-existing before the run, or made by another live
  session, from changes the suite made during this run, and fails the run only on the latter;
  the verdict is derived from a start-of-run snapshot of the guarded checkout, never from an
  unqualified `HEAD`/`git status` comparison.
- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate passed is not blocked
  by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout (modified, untracked and staged-shape paths all
  leave the verdict green and appear as informational notes).
- A genuine suite-caused mutation of a guarded checkout — above all a tracked-file
  deletion/wipe in the main checkout (the 2026-10-26 `packages/shared` incident class) — still
  fails the run: the fix narrows the false positive without weakening that protection.
- The derivation stays git-plumbing only (status codes plus the start snapshot); no `wl-*` or
  path-name heuristic is introduced, and `guarded_run_all` remains the single outer guard owner
  (the inner plugin applies the same helper, never a copy).
- Excluded main-checkout churn is never silent: it is rendered by `excluded_churn_notes` with
  the checkout path and status code (existing `EXCLUDED_CHURN_NOTE_PREFIX`) and surfaces as
  `live_repo_excluded` in the `run_tests.py` result JSON and text output.
- Cost stays bounded: no per-test work is added (the per-test fingerprint remains a trigger, and
  the narrowed bucket is computed once from the already-taken end snapshot).
- The tests from the test-first sibling pass, and the existing guarded-root pins stay green.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `diff_guarded_roots` (role-scoped post-process),
  `diff_snapshots`, `excluded_churn_notes`, `excluded_working_tree_churn`, module docstring
  rule statement, `MAIN_CHECKOUT_ROLE`/`GUARDED_ROOT_ROLE`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — verify it inherits the rule via `diff_guarded_roots`
  (no forked comparison).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_detect_live_repo_mutation` note plumbing.

## Constraints

- Fail closed: never turn a tracked-file deletion/wipe in any guarded checkout green.
- One rule, one owner: no second implementation in the inner plugin.
- Do not weaken refs/config coverage; do not touch the concurrency-excluded ref namespaces.

## Impact

A clean child session can no longer be failed, or blocked from finishing, by an unrelated sibling session's modified, untracked or staged-shape edits in the shared main checkout — those now surface as informational notes, while a genuine tracked-file wipe in a guarded checkout still fails the run.

# Name the concurrent actor on failures

**Parent:** WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC. **Depends on:** "Test: main-checkout churn verdict pins".
**Repo boundary:** **SorraAgents** skill tree (`skill/shared`, `skill/implement`, `skill/test`).

## Why

When the guard does fail (or reports excluded churn) the operator must be able to see *who* is
writing the shared checkout. Today the report implies the running item corrupted the tree, so an
operator hunts a phantom bug in a clean worktree. The producer chose option **(c)** for actor
detail: best-effort from durable evidence with an explicit `unknown` fallback — attribution is
**informational only** and never becomes a new failure mode.

## Scope

A best-effort, read-only evidence helper that names the likely owner of a dirty main-checkout
path. Evidence sources, in order, each optional:

1. `.implement_state.json` — the main checkout's own state file and registered sibling worktree
   state files (`<worktrees>/wl-*/​.implement_state.json`), i.e. the state file next to a
   candidate whose `repo_root`/worktree matches the main checkout.
2. Claimed work items — a `wl` lookup for items claimed by live sessions (bounded, cached per
   call, with a hard timeout).
3. The main-checkout lock holder metadata — `repo_lock.read_holder()` /
   `.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`.

Anything undiscoverable renders as `unknown`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the gate does fail, the report names the owning session/work item where one is
  discoverable (e.g. via `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the main-checkout lock
  holder), instead of implying the running item corrupted the tree.
- When no owner is discoverable the note says `unknown` explicitly and the run verdict is
  unchanged — attribution never flips a green run red or a red run green.
- The evidence helper is read-only, bounded (no unbounded `wl` calls, no per-test work, a
  documented timeout), and fail-open: any error or malformed state file degrades to `unknown`
  and is never raised into the verdict path.
- Attribution is a **documented second signal** appended to the note — never a substitute for
  the plumbing rule, and never a path-name/`wl-*` heuristic.
- A unit-tested `unknown` fallback covers: no state file, several candidate owners, unreadable
  JSON, and a lock held by an unrelated process.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/concurrent_actor.py` (new) or a documented function beside
  `excluded_churn_notes` in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — the evidence helper.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` (or `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrent_actor.py`) —
  helper unit tests, including the `unknown` fallbacks.
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `read_holder()` / `describe_holder()` reuse for lock-holder
  metadata.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `STATE_FILE_NAME` (`.implement_state.json`) shape,
  sibling state-file scan (`<worktrees>/wl-*/.implement_state.json`), and the existing
  finish-side attribution contract (`_main_checkout_guard_violations` /
  `_record_finish_own_churn`) that this helper must complement, never duplicate.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` — the sibling attribution
  pins (a deletion is never allow-listed) that must stay green.

## Constraints

- Informational only; no new failure mode (Q2 = c).
- No new subprocess in the per-test guard path; the helper runs only when building the
  finished-run note or the failure message.
- Never read or trust owner info to *excuse* a tracked-file deletion.

## Impact

When the guard fails or reports excluded churn, the operator now sees which live session or work item is writing the shared checkout (or an explicit `unknown`), so they can act on the real cause instead of hunting a phantom corruption bug in a clean worktree.

# Wire narrowed verdict through both guards

**Parent:** WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC. **Depends on:** "Role-scope the guard's verdict surface",
"Name the concurrent actor on failures".
**Repo boundary:** **SorraAgents** skill tree (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`,
`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

## Why

The narrowed rule and the actor evidence must reach the three consumers that decide whether a
driven child's `implement.py finish` pushes: the outer guard (`guarded_run_all` →
`_detect_live_repo_mutation`), the inner pytest plugin (`live_repo_guard`), and the finish gate
(`_adapt_guarded_result` / `_gate_failure_reason` / the finish report). Most plumbing exists
(`live_repo_excluded` is already carried and logged at INFO); this item makes the message and
the report state *what was excluded, why, and who likely wrote it* without forking the rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate passed is not blocked
  by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout: `implement.py finish` completes, and the
  excluded foreign paths (with the discovered owner or `unknown`) appear in the finish report
  and the log.
- A genuine suite-caused mutation of the guarded checkout — above all a tracked-file
  deletion/wipe in the main checkout — still fails the run: the finish gate still classifies
  `live_repo_mutation` as `GATE_FAILURE_INFRASTRUCTURE`, the failure text names every mutated
  checkout and path, and no excluded note hides it.
- Failure wording is honest: when a mutation is reported the text names the mutated checkout and
  paths and (where discoverable) the concurrent owner, instead of implying the running item
  corrupted the tree; excluded churn is labelled as excluded/foreign, not as damage.
- Both guards report the same verdict and the same notes for the same state (single shared
  helper; no second rule in `live_repo_guard.py`), proven by the parity test added in the
  test-first sibling.
- `run_tests.py` text output, its result JSON (`live_repo_excluded`, `live_repo_mutation`) and
  the implement gate all carry the notes; nothing is dropped silently.
- No change to guard ownership, the `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down, the `--collect-only`
  no-op, the xdist-worker no-op or the non-git no-op.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, `_detect_live_repo_mutation`,
  text/JSON rendering of `live_repo_excluded`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `pytest_runtest_teardown` / `pytest_sessionfinish`
  verdict + notes (must stay a pure consumer of the shared helper).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_adapt_guarded_result`, `_gate_failure_reason`,
  finish report `live_repo_excluded` surfacing, and the existing finish-side attribution
  contract it must dovetail with rather than duplicate: `_main_checkout_guard_violations`
  (`own_churn`, which never allow-lists a deletion), `_record_finish_own_churn`,
  `_main_checkout_guard_message`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`, `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` — wiring assertions and the
  existing attribution pins that must stay green.

## Constraints

- Exactly one outer guard owner; the inner plugin must not fork the rule.
- Fail closed; never push a checkout a suite-caused mutation corrupted.
- Bounded output: keep messages inside the existing tail/char budgets.
